title: Users and activation
hook: A toy service grows tenfold. What happens to activation when each cohort scales equally?

knows: basic arithmetic and the meaning of a percentage
doesNotKnow: Distinguish growth in the numerator from a change in the activation fraction when denominators grow proportionally.

misconception: A tenfold increase in activated users proves the activation process improved.
objective: Distinguish growth in the numerator from a change in the activation fraction when denominators grow proportionally.

claims.text: The named work is Lean Analytics, by Alistair Croll and Benjamin Yoskovitz, candidate publication year 2013.
claims.source: Alistair Croll and Benjamin Yoskovitz, Lean Analytics (2013); chapter (unconfirmed); edition and bibliography not independently opened. Access hold F1.

claims.text: Lean Analytics distinguishes metrics that inform a business model from attractive counts without enough context.
claims.source: Alistair Croll and Benjamin Yoskovitz, Lean Analytics (2013); chapter (unconfirmed); edition and bibliography not independently opened. Access hold F1.

claims.text: Original stipulated selection model: A inputs [10, 50, 10, 0] yield 25; B inputs [100, 50, 100, 0] yield 25. Prediction correct option 25. A and B both give {A}%. Scaling both cohorts tenfold scales activated users tenfold too, so the activation fraction does not improve. Cohort counts and rates are stipulated; no actual service or actionable-metric effect is measured.
claims.source: Original lesson construction; EDD-010 formula ; exact independent Python arithmetic recomputation recorded in answerCheck; no book dataset or measured human response.

claims.text: A toy product has 40 users at 75% activation and 40 at 25%. Overall expected activation percentage? Expected activations are 30 + 10 = 40 of 80 users, so the overall rate is 50%.
claims.source: Original transfer toy, selection, inputs [40, 75, 40, 25], output 50; independent Python recomputation.

claims.text: Does it hold up? Real-world applicability and the connection to the book remain unverified.
claims.source: Scope limitation, not a research verdict: only original toy derivation supplied. Publication requires independently opened book chapter and separate real-world evidence review; no effectiveness inference is made.

recall.question: A toy product has 40 users at 75% activation and 40 at 25%. Overall expected activation percentage?
recall.why: Expected activations are 30 + 10 = 40 of 80 users, so the overall rate is 50%.
